newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares end weak in rumour-driven trade.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares end weak in rumour-driven trade.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended weak in quiet trade on rumours, denied by central Reserve Bank and Finance Department, that announcement on foreign exchange controls may be made on Friday.
Golds finished soft on a sickly bullion price.

Dealers said there were also rumours in the market that the Reserve Bank may hike its key lending rate. This talk led to shares in the country's large commercial banks, Nedcor, Stanbic and First National sliding in late trade.
A central Bank rate hike will bring pressure to bear on banks to hike their lending rates.

Dealers said shares in Absa, South Africa's largest bank, were unscathed as it was seen the most resilient to a rate hike as it had issued long-term loans in the money market, while other banks had issued short-term loans.
Investors were on Friday seen dumping rand-hedge stocks, bought earlier in the week, as the rand gained strength. Players were also seen squaring positions ahead of the weekend.
Dealers said volumes were thin in a quiet market, although the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said this week saw the highest ever trading value recorded on the bourse in its 109-year history.
The overall index lost 3.9 points to 6,971.4 points, the industrial index shed 15.1 points to 8,194.1 and golds dropped 9.8 points to 1,722.5 points.
